title: Oil Settles Near $100 as Hormuz Flows Stunt Rally
title_cn: Oil Settles Near $100 as Hormuz Flows Stunt Rally
summary:
Oil fell Monday, settling near $100 a barrel, on signs Saudi Arabia is boosting exports via the key Strait of Hormuz and fresh hopes for diplomatic progress in the Iran war. Brent, the global benchmark, declined for a fourth session, settling 3.4% lower. The October West Texas Intermediate contract, which expires on Tuesday, fell about 4.5%. Satellite data showed that Saudi Arabia’s observed oil loadings from inside the Persian Gulf jumped over the weekend, with the highest number of ships seen at the nation’s main Persian Gulf port since June. The images indicate that the kingdom is successfully redirecting its exports back toward the Gulf following the shutdown of its vital East-West pipeline due to drone attacks. 

For more, we speak with Humayun Tai, Global Leader of Energy & Materials at McKinsey. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Bitcoin Reaches Eight-Month High After Clarity Act Loss
title_cn: Bitcoin Reaches Eight-Month High After Clarity Act Loss
summary:
Bloomberg Intelligence Senior US Policy Analyst Nathan Dean discusses the Securities and Exchange Commission giving the green light for digital versions of securities to start trading in the US. This plan could reshape traditional market structure after crypto legislation failed a key Senate vote on Tuesday.

Also affecting the crypto space, Bitcoin surged past $85,000 to its highest since late-January, extending a sharp rebound as falling oil prices and a broader return of risk appetite helped cryptocurrencies move past setbacks on US crypto legislation and monetary policy. The original cryptocurrency climbed as much as 6.5% to $86,331 in New York trading, almost $10,000 above the lows touched last week after the Clarity Act stalled and the Federal Reserve raised interest rates. Even after that rebound, Bitcoin remains roughly a third below its record last October. Nathan Dean speaks with Bloomberg's Joe Mathieu on Balance of Power. (Source: Bloomberg)
